title: Assessment and Testing Strategies
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: Assessment and Testing Strategies.

items: Security assessments evaluate the effectiveness of security controls
Assessments should be regular, planned, and documented
Include technical and non-technical evaluation methods
Results drive risk-based decisions about security improvements
Must cover people, processes, and technology

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: Security assessment and testing involves "identifying organizational goals, critical systems, and the controls in place to mitigate risks to those goals or systems. As always, balancing the cost of measuring with the benefits is critical." Types of security assessments:

items: Vulnerability assessments — Identify weaknesses
Penetration tests — Exploit weaknesses to prove impact
Security audits — Verify compliance with policies and standards
Risk assessments — Evaluate likelihood and impact of threats
Configuration reviews — Verify systems meet baseline standards
Internal assessments — Conducted by the organization's own security team
External assessments — Conducted by independent third parties
External assessments provide objectivity and credibility
Internal assessments offer deeper organizational knowledge
Many compliance frameworks require external assessments

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Regulatory compliance often requires EXTERNAL (independent) assessments. Internal assessments are valuable but may not satisfy compliance requirements because they lack independence.

items: Independent evaluation of an organization's controls
SOC reports — Most common third-party audit framework
Results shared with customers, regulators, and stakeholders
Provides assurance without requiring individual customer audits
Based on AICPA standards (SSAE 18 in the U.S.)

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: Third-party assessments allow "the organization to conduct an external assessment instead of multiple third-party assessments and then sharing the resulting report with customers and potential customers." "Outside of the United States, similar engagements are conducted under the International Standard on Assurance Engagements (ISAE) 3402."
